draft.title: Source documents
card: A source document is the first record of a transaction. It proves the transaction happened and gives the details to record, such as the date, amount and who was involved.
Receipt
proof that money was received or paid. A business gives one to a customer who pays, and keeps the copy.
Invoice
a bill for goods or services sold on credit. It shows what was sold, the amount owed and when payment is due.
Cheque butt and bank statement
a cheque butt is the stub kept in the cheque book, showing the date, payee and amount of a cheque written. A bank statement is the bank's record of money paid into and out of the account.
draft.remember: Every entry starts with a document that proves it happened.

a.q: A plumber finishes a job and sends the customer a bill, with payment due in 30 days. Which source document is this?
a.why: An invoice is a bill for goods or services sold on credit, showing the amount owed and the due date. A receipt would only be given once money was actually paid.
a.clue: The customer has not paid yet.

b.q: Tom writes a cheque to pay a supplier. Which document in his cheque book gives him the date, payee and amount for his records?
b.why: The cheque butt is the stub kept in the cheque book and shows the details of the cheque he wrote. A bank statement comes from the bank later and is not kept in the cheque book.
b.clue: Look for the part that stays in the book.

b.q: Tom pays a supplier by cheque. As he writes it, he fills in the date, payee and amount on a document he keeps. Which is it?
